claude.sample_unit: model outputs annotated by 18 medical experts (80,502 annotations; 200 queries)

links.outcome: Factuality and completeness of RAG vs non-RAG LLM responses, expert-rated
links.effect: Standard RAG often degraded performance: factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5% versus non-RAG; only 22% of top-16 passages relevant; evidence selection precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%.
links.quote: Contrary to expectation, standard RAG often degraded performance: only 22% of top-16 passages were relevant, evidence selection remained weak (precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%), and factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5%, respectively, compared with non-RAG variants.

screen.practice: retrieval grounding with evidence filtering and query reformulation
screen.reason: This study systematically evaluates the implementation of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and specific RAG safeguards/modifications (evidence filtering, query reformulation) compared to standard LLM generation on clinical questions using expert human evaluation.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) vs non-RAG, evidence filtering, and query reformulation
